_what_this_is: Adversarial regressions for the genesis validation driver, the aggregation authority and
the identities the genesis verifier binds. The driver runs exactly one stage per invocation,
so isolation is delegated to one disposable runner per stage; the aggregator must then refuse
unless every stage arrives exactly once, from the same commit, tree, driver and recipe.

defects.why: A failed stage could still contribute measurements, so printed text would outrank the exit code.
An ambiguous marker would resolve to its first match, which is the log-spoofing hole the driver exists to close.

defects.why: A stage that never reported a measurement would silently contribute zero.
The driver could measure a tree other than the commit being authorized.
A dirty or stale checkout would be measured instead of failing closed.

defects.why: The aggregator would emit a passing result even though stages failed.
A result assembled by an unpinned aggregator could authorize genesis.
Evidence produced without per-runner stage isolation could authorize genesis.
A run of some other workflow commit could be presented as the authoritative ladder.
A run of altered workflow content could be presented as the authoritative ladder.
The genesis application stage would run the factory suite again, duplicating the family the factory stage owns.
The genesis application stage would fall back to the integrated runner and measure the factory family twice.
The pinned validation artifacts would be believed from the candidate-produced result rather than recomputed from the object store.
